Goodman–Kruskal's Gamma

Source: R/gkGamma.R
gkGamma.Rd

Computes Goodman–Kruskal's Gamma, a measure of association for ordinal variables. The function provides interfaces for both contingency tables and paired vectors.

gkGamma(x, y = NULL, conf.level = NA, ...)

Arguments

x

numeric vector or a contingency table (matrix or table)

y

optional numeric vector. If supplied, it must have the same length as x.

conf.level

confidence level for the interval. If NA, no confidence interval is returned.

...

further arguments passed to table in the vector interface

Value

if conf.level = NA, a numeric scalar. Otherwise a named numeric vector with elements:

est

point estimate of Goodman-Kruskal's gamma

lci

lower confidence interval bound

uci

upper confidence interval bound

Details

Goodman–Kruskal's Gamma is based solely on the number of concordant and discordant pairs and ignores ties. It is defined as

$$ \gamma = \frac{C - D}{C + D} $$

where \(C\) and \(D\) denote the number of concordant and discordant pairs.

Gamma takes values in \([-1, 1]\). Values close to \(1\) indicate strong positive association, values close to \(-1\) strong negative association.

In contrast to Kendall's \(\tau_b\) and Somers' D, Gamma ignores ties, which can lead to overestimation of association when ties are present.

For \(2 \times 2\) tables, Gamma is equivalent to Yule's Q (yuleQ).

Gamma is symmetric: gkGamma(x, y) = gkGamma(y, x).

References

Agresti, A. (2002) Categorical Data Analysis. John Wiley & Sons, pp. 57–59.

Brown, M. B., & Benedetti, J. K. (1977). Sampling behavior of tests for correlation in two-way contingency tables. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 72, 309–315.

Goodman, L. A., & Kruskal, W. H. (1954). Measures of association for cross classifications. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 49, 732–764.

Goodman, L. A., & Kruskal, W. H. (1963). Measures of association for cross classifications III. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 58, 310–364.

See also

yuleQ for \(2 \times 2\) tables

Other assoc.ordinal: cStat(), conDisPairs(), gkTau(), kendallTauA(), kendallTauB(), kendallW(), somersDelta(), stuartTauC()

Examples


# Example from SAS documentation (PROC FREQ)
# https://support.sas.com/documentation/

tab <- as.table(rbind(
  c(26,26,23,18, 9),
  c( 6, 7, 9,14,23)
))

gkGamma(tab, conf.level=0.95)
#>       est       lci       uci 
#> 0.5313123 0.3479918 0.7146328 

# Vector interface
gkGamma(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
#> [1] -0.7360825
